benefits.title: Long-term memory per user, millions of tenants
benefits.body: Short-term memory lives in the context window; long-term memory lands here as rows: millions of tenants per collection via partition key, or 65,536 collections for separate schemas.

benefits.title: Permissions agents can't bypass
benefits.body: RBAC gives each agent or tool its own role. Row-level security is available only in Zilliz Cloud enterprise edition.

benefits.title: Hybrid search plus grep
benefits.body: Combine dense and BM25 retrieval with regex, LIKE, and phrase filters, then rerank, in one request.

feature_blocks.title: Long-term agent memory at million-tenant scale
feature_blocks.body: Use agent_id, user_id or session_id as the partition key to organize millions of tenants in one collection. Include the tenant filter on every request. Episodic, semantic and procedural memories can use a type field; separate collections when schemas or permission boundaries differ.
bullets: Include the tenant filter on every request; partition-key pruning reduces the data scanned.
65,536 collections and 64 databases per cluster by default, configurable.
Forgetting built in: Entity TTL (Milvus 3.0+) expires memories on schedule; delete by filter erases one user on request.

feature_blocks.title: RBAC for agents, plus row-level security in the enterprise edition
feature_blocks.body: Open-source Milvus provides users, roles and privileges at instance, database and collection levels. Row-level security is available only in Zilliz Cloud enterprise edition; a partition key is not an authorization mechanism.
bullets: Built-in groups such as COLL_RO and COLL_RW, or custom privilege groups.
Configure row-level policies and caller identity for the enterprise deployment.

feature_blocks.title: Hybrid search for agent memory, with grep
feature_blocks.body: Agents need meaning and exact strings: error codes, file paths, order numbers. Regex filters run alone or inside hybrid search.
bullets: Dense + sparse/BM25 hybrid search with RRF or weighted rerankers.
Regex =~ / !~ (RE2, Milvus 3.0+) and LIKE, accelerated by NGRAM index.
TEXT_MATCH, PHRASE_MATCH, TEXT_MATCH_FUZZY, and JSON path filters.

feature_blocks.title: Your memory framework, and MCP
feature_blocks.body: Milvus is the agent memory layer under the frameworks agents already use; an MCP server for agents lets Claude Desktop or Cursor query it directly.
bullets: Mem0, Letta (MemGPT), Agno, OpenAI Agents SDK, LangChain and LlamaIndex integrations in the docs.
MCP tools for vector, text and hybrid search, query, insert and delete.
Embedding Functions (Milvus 2.6+) call OpenAI, Cohere, Voyage AI and others on insert and query.

code.h2: Can agents search like grep and by meaning at once?
code.intro: Recall one user's memories that match a regex, ranked by dense and BM25 retrieval fused with RRF.
code.code:
from pymilvus import MilvusClient, AnnSearchRequest, RRFRanker

client = MilvusClient(uri="http://localhost:19530", token="root:Milvus")
question = "what did we promise about the refund?"
scope = 'user_id == "u42" and content =~ "(?i)refund.*order [0-9]+"'

# embed() stands for your embedding model; it returns a list of floats.
dense = AnnSearchRequest(data=[embed(question)], anns_field="dense",
                         param={}, limit=20, expr=scope)
# BM25 sparse field generated from content: pass the raw query text.
sparse = AnnSearchRequest(data=[question], anns_field="sparse",
                          param={}, limit=20, expr=scope)

hits = client.hybrid_search(
    collection_name="agent_memory",
    reqs=[dense, sparse],
    ranker=RRFRanker(),
    limit=5,
    output_fields=["content"],
)
code.note: Assumes user_id as the partition key, a VARCHAR content field, a dense vector field, and a BM25 sparse field. Add an NGRAM index on content to speed up the regex. Code requires a running server and your own embedding model; it is an example, not a benchmark.

faqs: What is the best database for AI agents?

One that isolates memory per user at scale, enforces permissions in the database and answers semantic and exact-string queries. Milvus does all three open source; Zilliz Cloud adds row-level security.
Do AI agents need a vector database, or is Postgres enough?

Stateful agents need a system of record and a memory layer. Keep orders and billing in your transactional database; put memories, documents and tool results in Milvus, with tenant-scoped hybrid search and per-row expiry built in.
What is the difference between short-term and long-term agent memory? How do AI agents remember things between sessions?

Short-term vs long-term agent memory: short-term is the context window and ends with the session; long-term persists across sessions as rows, an embedding plus user_id, timestamp, memory type (episodic, semantic, procedural) and source, recalled by tenant-scoped hybrid search.
How should AI agents forget outdated information?
Three ways: upsert replaces a memory by primary key, Entity TTL (Milvus 3.0+) expires rows on a schedule, and delete by filter erases everything for one user_id, honoring a deletion request.
How do I prevent cross-tenant data leakage in AI agents?

Scope data, not prompts: a partition key per tenant, RBAC roles per agent or tool, and on Zilliz Cloud row-level security filtering every read and write by caller, so a prompt injection cannot widen the scope.
Is agent memory the same as RAG?
No. RAG retrieves shared documents the agent did not write; memory is per user, written by the agent as it runs. Milvus holds both with the same hybrid search and filters.

notes: "百万表" (one million collections/tables) is UNVERIFIED and not claimed. Checked 2026-10-21: milvus.io multi_tenancy.md (v3.0.x docs) says 65,536 collections per cluster by default, raisable via maxCollectionNum, and 'millions of tenants' only for the partition-key strategy; configs/milvus.yaml on origin/3.0 has maxCollectionNum 65536 / maxCollectionNumPerDB 65536 / maxDatabaseNum 64 / maxPartitionNum 1024; GitHub issue/PR search for 'million collections', '1M collections', 'massive collections', 'lightweight collection' found no feature or release note (only perf work such as #33236 '10k collections', #49587 / #51915 mention 100k collections in internal optimization context); Zilliz Cloud docs/limits caps collections at min(1,024 x CUs, 16,384) per cluster and docs/multi-tenancy says 'up to 16,384 collections' and partition key 'millions of tenants'. Page therefore says 'millions of tenants per collection via partition key' + '65,536 collections by default (configurable)'. If engineering wants to publish a 1M-collection claim, it needs a released doc/benchmark first.

Row-level security is framed as an enterprise capability via Zilliz Cloud per owner direction (2026-10-21), not as an open-source Milvus feature; the open-source 'RLS in 3.0.3' proof chip was removed. docs.zilliz.com has no RLS page (docs/row-level-security 404, not in sitemap, not in docs/multi-tenancy). Confirm Zilliz Cloud RLS availability, plan tier and product name before launch, then link its docs page.

RLS behavior described (per-collection policies, filters bound to the calling principal and its tags, enforced on reads and writes, fail-closed) follows the Milvus RLS design doc 20250610-rls_design.md; re-check against the Zilliz Cloud docs once published.

On Milvus 3.0.x, LIKE and regex apply to VARCHAR fields, JSON string paths, and a specified ARRAY<VARCHAR> element (e.g. tags[0]) — not TEXT fields (pattern-matching.md). Regex =~/!~ requires Milvus 3.0+; NGRAM requires 2.6+; (?i) regex may skip NGRAM optimization.

Code assumes collection agent_memory with user_id (VARCHAR, partition key), content (VARCHAR with analyzer enabled), a dense float vector field 'dense' and a BM25-function output sparse field 'sparse'. AnnSearchRequest(expr=...) and hybrid_search(reqs, ranker, limit) per multi-vector-search.md; RRFRanker is the pymilvus helper for the 'rrf' reranker.

Entity TTL (per-row expiration via a TIMESTAMPTZ field) is a Milvus 3.0 feature per release_notes.md; element-level partial update of JSON paths is in 3.0.3 for Go SDK and REST v2 only, so the page says 'partial update' generically.
FMINDEX removed (master-only, not in a released version).
Customer stories specific to agent memory: wanted, unverified. Logos are from the verified homepage adopter list, not claims of agent-memory use.
